newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian minister seen shedding light on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian minister seen shedding light on Busang.

text.p: Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana was expected to shed some light on the Busang gold find saga when he appears before a parliamentary commission, industry sources said Tuesday.
Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd, which discovered the find, is being pushed by the Indonesian government to link up with Barrick Gold Corp., another Canadian mining company, to develop the property.

The sources said that while there was no fixed agenda for the routine commission hearing Wednesday, legislators were expected to raise questions related to the Busang find, which is estimated to contain some 57 million ounces of gold worth about $21 billion.
"It is expected to be a very interesting meeting," said one source who has been following closely the drawn out dispute.

The government sent the two Canadian firms a letter dated Nov. 22 asking Bre-X to retain a 25 percent stake in the property, with Barrick taking 75 percent. The companies have been advised to allocate a 10 percent stake to the Indonesian government.
Mines and Energy Ministry Secretary-General Umar Said said Monday that Bre-X and Barrick had agreed to the contents of the letter, but Bre-X said no deal had been completed.
The sources said the legislators were expected to seek a clarification from Sudjana on the current status of the Busang property and when its development was likely to begin.
